newsitem.title: USA: Boeing considers freighter version of 737.
newsitem.headline: Boeing considers freighter version of 737.

text.p: Boeing Co is considering producing a freighter version of its new generation 737-700 jet, a company executive said Thursday.
Joseph Ozimek, director of product marketing for Boeing's commercial airplane group, told reporters at a briefing that a decision on the possible new jet would likely be made by the end of the year
But he said that if the company were to approve the new model, he did not expect it would be produced until after the year 2000.
Ozimek said a new freighter version of the new 737 probably would carry eight cargo pallets weighing about 15 tons, and would have a range of about 1,500 miles.
"It's something we see as a reasonable opportunity," he said. "It's not high on the priority list."
Ozimek said that a freighter version of the 777 model was less likely in the near future, mainly because of high demand for passenger versions of the new wide-bodied jet.
Boeing currently is producing freight versions of its 747, 757 and 767 models. Boeing produced freighter versions of its 737-200 model from the early 1970s through the mid-1980s, Ozimek said.
He also said a potential future version of the 737 freighter would replace current 737-200 freighters, 727 freighters and other jets.
